verified.exploit_entry_point: The real CLI tools (ansible / ansible-playbook / ansible-console) run an ad-hoc debug task that prints the connection password made available to the run. The prompted form is driven through a pseudo-terminal (the real getpass path); the automation forms are ordinary subprocess invocations. Every fix layer (source wrapping, string conversion, templating guard) is exercised through those tools.
sites: lib/ansible/cli/__init__.py:251-279 (ask_passwords; prompted connection and become passwords leave as to_bytes values at the pin)
lib/ansible/playbook/play_context.py:160-173 (the automation-facing password sources added to the baseline: file and environment)

lib/ansible/playbook/play_context.py:164,170 and lib/ansible/playbook/base.py:342 (PlayContext.post_validate templates every string attribute; get_validated_value then converts the value with to_text)
lib/ansible/template/__init__.py:229-246 (_is_unsafe only recognises unsafe values that are string_types)
lib/ansible/utils/unsafe_proxy.py:64-90 (AnsibleUnsafeText; no bytes counterpart and no encode/decode preservation at the pin)
routes: T1 prompted connection password containing template syntax, including an embedded expression surrounded by ordinary text
T2 connection password supplied through the environment with surrounding whitespace

traps.shape: the connection password typed at the prompt is converted to bytes and left unprotected, so template syntax embedded anywhere in it is expanded by the template engine; coupled must-keep-working: ordinary and non-ASCII passwords are used verbatim, and ordinary template expressions still render
traps.reason_to_dismiss: getpass already hides the typed input and the value looks like ordinary data, so it is assumed the secret cannot be executable; the project's own byte conversion reads as normal normalisation.
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (GHSA-cqmr-rcpr-cxh3, completed by GHSA-6fq2-x65v-v9h7); the prompt form is the advisory's own route

traps.shape: the connection password supplied through the environment is stripped and handed on as plain text, so template syntax is expanded; coupled must-keep-working: surrounding whitespace is still trimmed and a password file still takes precedence
traps.reason_to_dismiss: environment values are read as operator configuration rather than as a prompt, so they look like data; the advisory names prompts.
traps.realistic_because: injected: an automation-facing password source of the kind the project added later; reachable through the real CLI and covered only by the general property

traps.shape: the connection password read from a file is stripped as bytes and wrapped in the wrong string type, or wrapped before the trim, so the unsafe marker is lost in the byte-to-text conversion; the file may use a trailing CRLF or non-ASCII text; coupled must-keep-working: the trailing newline is still trimmed and a prompted password still takes precedence
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a file holds a literal secret and bytes look like the natural result of reading it; wrapping the bytes, or wrapping before trimming the newline, appears equivalent to wrapping the text.
traps.realistic_because: injected: mirrors the password-file option the project shipped later; reachable through the real CLI and covered only by the general property

A.summary: Passwords read from a prompt are expanded as templates when used, exposing or changing the secret

B.summary: Incomplete fix for CVE-2019-10206: the unsafe marker is lost when the password is converted from bytes to text
